fact: Evans's zoning code says areas where animals are kept must not create odors, dust, noise or drainage that is a hazard or nuisance to adjoining properties.
quote: Areas in which animals are maintained shall not create odors, dust, noise or drainage which constitutes a hazard or nuisance to adjoining properties or uses.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 18.02.040.J.1, accessory uses: household pets (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)
notes: Read via the Municode API (job 487488) on 2026-09-25. Title 18; Ord. 865-26 (ADUs, July 2026) amended Title 18 after this codification and may touch 18.02.040.B, not read.

fact: Evans's animal code says areas where animals are kept must be maintained so they do not create odors, dust, noise or drainage offensive to neighbors.
quote: Areas in which animals are kept shall be maintained in a manner which does not create odors, dust, noise or drainage offensive to the senses of smell, hearing, or sight, thereby constituting a hazard or nuisance to the use or enjoyment of adjoining properties.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 6.04.140(B), nuisance animals (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)
notes: Ord. No. 867-26, amending Chapter 6.04, passed second reading on July 21, 2026 and is not yet in the online code; its text was not available to read (only the published title). Re-read this section once Municode codifies it.

fact: The City of Evans says no household may keep a combined total of more than four pet animals, requires a City Clerk license with proof of current rabies vaccination for each dog or cat six months or older, and does not ban specific dog breeds.
quote: No license shall be required for any dog or cat under the age of six months. No license shall be required for seeing eye dogs. The City does not ban specific dog breeds. … It is unlawful for any owner, keeper, harborer, or any other person to keep, maintain, harbor or possess in any one household, a combined total of more than four pet animals within the City of Evans.
source_label: City of Evans, Animal Licensing (page read September 25, 2026)
notes: Current city page, read after Ord. 867-26 passed (July 21, 2026). Code source: Sec. 6.04.300(K), 'more than four (4) pet or fowl animals'.

fact: Evans lets a household ask the City Council for a variance from its limit of four pet or fowl animals, decided after a public hearing noticed at least 10 days ahead, on criteria that include no unreasonable noise or smell and a fit with the size, shape, topography and location of the property.
quote: Keep, maintain, harbor or possess in any one household, a combined total of more than four (4) pet or fowl animals within the City. … The City Council shall hold a public hearing and make the final decision to grant the requested variance, grant a variance with a lesser number of animals than the request, or deny the variance. Notice of the public hearing shall be published at least ten (10) days prior to the hearing in a newspaper of general circulation in the City and notice of the public hearing shall be posted on the premises at least ten (10) days prior to such hearing. … 2. The variance will not result in damage to adjoining properties, nor an unreasonable amount of noise or smell, and will not otherwise be materially detrimental to the public welfare; and 3. The variance is appropriate, given the size, shape, topography and/or location of the property upon which the animals are to be kept.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 6.04.300(K), animal care (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)
notes: Ord. No. 867-26, amending Chapter 6.04, passed second reading on July 21, 2026 and is not yet in the online code; its text was not available to read (only the published title). Re-read this section once Municode codifies it.

fact: At its April 21, 2026 meeting the Evans City Council held a public hearing on an animal variance application.
quote: The council will hold a Public Hearing and will consider Resolution 04-2026 related to an animal variance application.
source_label: City of Evans news post, April 21, 2026: City Council meeting and work session agenda
notes: Agenda preview only; the outcome of Resolution 04-2026 was not read (packets are on a portal that did not load).

fact: In Evans a dog is running at large when it is neither on its owner's premises nor on a leash of 10 feet or less held by or tied to a person.
quote: A dog shall be considered running at large when it is neither on the premises of the owner nor on a leash ten (10) feet or less in length, attached to the dog and held by or tied to a person.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 6.04.020(B), control required (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)
notes: Ord. No. 867-26, amending Chapter 6.04, passed second reading on July 21, 2026 and is not yet in the online code; its text was not available to read (only the published title). Re-read this section once Municode codifies it.

fact: Evans requires a dog's owner to remove its feces immediately from public property and from any private property other than the owner's own.
quote: Any owner, taking the animal upon any public way or other public property in the City, shall immediately remove or cause to be removed, and lawfully dispose of all fecal matter left on such property by the animal. … Any owner, taking any animal upon any private property other than his or her own, shall immediately remove or cause to be removed, and lawfully dispose of all fecal matter left on such property by the animal.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 6.04.130, animal defecation (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)
notes: Ord. No. 867-26, amending Chapter 6.04, passed second reading on July 21, 2026 and is not yet in the online code; its text was not available to read (only the published title). Re-read this section once Municode codifies it.

fact: On July 21, 2026 the Evans City Council passed on second reading an ordinance amending the city's animal-control chapter.
quote: The following Ordinance passed on the second reading at a regular meeting of the Evans City Council held on July 21, 2026. … ORDINANCE NO. 867-26 AN ORDINANCE AMENDING TITLE 6, CHAPTER 6.04 OF THE EVANS MUNICIPAL CODE REGARDING ANIMAL CONTROL
source_label: City of Evans legal notice, Ordinance No. 867-26, second reading July 21, 2026
notes: The notice carries the title only. Municode's OrdBank lists 867-26 as not yet codified (checked 2026-09-25).

fact: Evans zoning defines a kennel as commercial or institutional property keeping four or more pet animals at least four months old for training, boarding or breeding, requires drainage improvements that protect storm sewers and nearby waters, and lists kennels in the AG, C-3, I-2 and I-3 districts, with special use approval in C-1, C-2 and I-1.
quote: Kennel - any property used for commercial or institutional purposes, on which four (4) or more pet animals, at least four (4) months of age, are kept for training, boarding or breeding, whether in special structures, runs or not, subject to the following: a. Waste shall be handled and disposed of in a sanitary manner approved by the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment. … c. Drainage facilities or improvements shall be constructed to protect municipal storm sewers and adjacent rivers and bodies of water.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 18.02.020, allowed uses, Table 18-2-1 and use definitions (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)
notes: Table 18-2-1 read cell by cell from the Municode HTML: Kennel ■ in AG, C3, I2, I3; S in C1, C2, I1; blank in PF and every residential district.

fact: Evans does not allow veterinary clinics, animal hospitals or kennels to run as home occupations.
quote: The following uses, regardless of whether they meet the performance standards, are not permitted. … i. Veterinary clinics, animal hospitals or kennels.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 18.02.040.K.12, prohibited home occupations (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)

fact: Evans limits a fence in a required front yard setback to 4 feet and other residential fences to 6 feet, and counts chain link among allowed fence materials.
quote: Fences and walls which are located in required front yard setbacks shall not exceed four (4) feet in height above adjoining grade, except in industrial zone districts. … Other fences and walls shall not exceed six (6) feet in height as measured vertically from the surrounding grade … All fencing shall be constructed of brick, wood pickets, vinyl, wrought iron, decorative concrete block, steel, chain link or other material normally used for fencing
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 18.02.040.H, fences, walls and hedges (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)

fact: Freedom Dog Park, at 2095 42nd Street, is the only dog park on the City of Evans parks list and has separate areas for large dogs and for small or timid dogs, plus an agility training area.
quote: At Freedom Dog Park, there are separate dog park areas available for large dogs, small/timid dogs, and an agility training area.
source_label: City of Evans, Parks (Freedom Dog Park, 2095 42nd Street)
notes: The city's park description does not use the words off-leash; the off-leash rule is Sec. 16.40.112 (evans-co.code-16-40-112-off-leash).

fact: Evans closed Freedom Dog Park beginning May 25, 2026 while Chevron plugged and abandoned an oil and gas well near the park.
quote: Freedom Dog Park is temporarily closed beginning May 25 while Chevron Energy completes plugging, abandoning and shut-in work on an oil and gas well near the park.
source_label: City of Evans news post, May 26, 2026: Freedom Dog Park temporarily closed

fact: On August 31, 2026 Evans announced that Freedom Dog Park had reopened after Chevron finished work on its former well sites near the park ahead of schedule.
quote: Freedom Dog Park has reopened to the public after Chevron completed work on its former well sites near the park ahead of schedule.
source_label: City of Evans news post, Aug. 31, 2026: Freedom Dog Park reopens

fact: Evans requires a multifamily development of more than 12 units to provide common areas, one for every three buildings or 100 units, whichever is less, each with at least three listed features, among them a play structure for children 5 to 12 and a dog relief area.
quote: Multifamily developments providing over twelve (12) dwelling units require common areas within each site. One (1) common area is required for every three (3) buildings or every hundred (100) units, whichever is less. Each common area shall contain at least three (3) of the following, not to include a stormwater detention pond, but may include: … g. Play structure intended for children ages five (5) to twelve (12). … j. Dog relief area.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 18.05.050.B, lot open space: multifamily common areas (Ord. 804-23, 2023) (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)

fact: New or substantially improved residential front yards in Evans must meet landscape minimums by frontage type: at least 60% landscape on terrace frontages, 75% on neighborhood frontages and 50% on suburban frontages; Table 18-5-2 makes suburban the first-preference frontage in R-1, and the first preference applies unless site constraints prevent it.
quote: Front yard landscape. All new or substantially improved residential front yard landscaping shall comply with the percentages in Table 18-5-3 and shall comply with Section 18.05.050 , Lot open space. … Front Yard Landscape: 60% minimum landscape; and 40% maximum hardscape. | 75% minimum landscape; and 25% maximum hardscape. | 50% minimum landscape; and 50% maximum hardscape … The frontage of first preference shall be applied unless site constraints, such as utility location or lot size, prevent application.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 18.05.030, frontages, Table 18-5-3 (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)
notes: Columns of Table 18-5-3: Terrace 60/40, Neighborhood 75/25, Suburban 50/50, Buffer (landscape buffer types). Table 18-5-2 makes Suburban the first-preference frontage in R-1. The code does not say whether artificial turf counts as landscape or hardscape.

fact: The City of Evans set its 31st annual golf tournament, a four-person scramble, for July 24, 2026 at Eaton Country Club.
quote: The 31st Annual City of Evans Golf Tournament will tee off on Friday, July 24, at Eaton Country Club, bringing together local businesses, community members, and golf enthusiasts for a day of friendly competition, networking, and fun.
source_label: City of Evans news post, June 18, 2026: 31st annual golf tournament set for July 24 at Eaton Country Club

fact: The City of Evans parks page lists 16 parks and open spaces, none of them a golf course; Pioneer Park in Ashcroft Heights has a nine-hole disc golf course, and ten parks list playgrounds.
quote: Located in the Ashcroft Heights Subdivision and adjacent to the Fox Crossing Condos, Pioneer Park offers two playgrounds, a nine hole disc golf course, walking paths, picnic area, and a large open turf/grass area.
source_label: City of Evans, Parks (16 listed parks and open spaces, read September 25, 2026)
notes: Counted 2026-09-25: Arrowhead OS, Charles H. Welch, City Park, Dante, DaVinci, Driftwood, Freedom Dog Park, Green Meadows OS, Hunter's Reserve, Pioneer, Prairie View, Renaissance, Ridge, Riverside, Village, Vineyard. Playgrounds listed at City, Driftwood, Hunter's Reserve, Pioneer (two), Prairie View, Renaissance, Ridge, Riverside, Village, Vineyard (two). No golf course listed.

fact: When Evans voters approved a local sales tax on food on November 5, 2002, the capital projects it could pay for included a municipal golf course.
quote: On November 5, 2002, Evans electors approved a local sales tax on domestic food, the revenue derived therefrom, to be used for the purpose of capital improvement projects to local park and recreation facilities, trails and walkways, streets, bridges, traffic control, that may include but not be limited to: Ashcroft Heights and Hunter's Reserve neighborhood parks; Improvement of 37th Street West of 35th Avenue; Riverside Trail Expansion; Expansion to Evans Community Complex Including in an Indoor Aquatic Center; Municipal Golf Course.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 3.04.1060, local sales tax on domestic food (Ord. 769-22, 2022) (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)
notes: Voters widened the allowed uses in 2021 (Ballot Issue 2B, police station). No golf course appears on the city's parks list in 2026.

fact: Every new Evans residential subdivision must give residents neighborhood identity features, one for 12 to 50 units up to four for more than 300; a playground with commercial-grade equipment counts as one, other features need City Council approval, and features not dedicated to the City are common area the owners association maintains in perpetuity.
quote: Twelve (12) to fifty (50) units: One (1) feature. … More than three hundred (300) units: Four (4) common areas. … d. Playgrounds with commercial-grade equipment, picnic/barbeque areas with commercial-grade equipment, or court games (tennis, volleyball or basketball) at least one thousand (1,000) square feet in area shall each count as one (1) identity feature. … h. Other features may be considered credit toward meeting the identity feature requirement, subject to approval by the City Council. 3. All neighborhood identity features not dedicated or not eligible for dedication to the City shall be considered common area and shall be maintained in perpetuity by the owners association, unless otherwise stated herein.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 18.04.070.E, neighborhood identity features (Ord. 804-23, 2023) (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)
notes: Full scale: 12-50 units one feature; 51-150 two; 151-300 three; over 300 four. The option list (a-g) names trails, pocket parks, water features or art, playgrounds/picnic/court games, plazas or gardens, a community building, a pool or splash park; a putting green is not listed.

fact: Evans's landscape design chapter, re-enacted by Ord. 804-23 on October 17, 2023, applies to the common and public areas of new subdivisions, new or substantially amended site plans, new or substantially improved multifamily and nonresidential structures and parking lots, and infill and rehabilitation of existing sites, where the Director may prorate the standards.
quote: Construction or development of a site in one of the following categories shall not be undertaken until a landscape plan that meets or exceeds the standards of this Chapter has been approved by the Director. This shall apply to the following: a. Common and public areas of any new major or minor subdivision. b. New or substantially amended site plans. c. New or substantially improved multifamily and nonresidential structures. d. New or substantially improved parking lots. e. Infill and rehabilitation of existing sites. The Director may prorate the requirements to the extent of the development or site work, where full compliance is not possible or practical, and only apply the standards to portions of the site subject to development.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 18.08.010.B, landscape applicability (chapter enacted by Ord. 804-23, Oct. 17, 2023) (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)
notes: Editor's note on Ch. 18.08: Ord. 804-23, § 2(Exh. A), adopted Oct. 17, 2023, repealed the former Ch. 18.08 and enacted the current one. A single-family backyard on an existing lot is not in the list.

fact: In a new Evans park, between 15% and 50% of the park area must be designed for active, programmed or structured recreation such as ball fields, playgrounds or sport courts, and every open space must also meet the city's landscape design chapter.
quote: Open spaces shall be designed according to the following guidelines for each specific type in addition to meeting the applicable standards in Chapter 18.08 , Landscape Design. … Between fifteen (15) percent and fifty (50) percent of the park area shall be designed for active, programmed or structured recreation such as ball fields, playgrounds or sport courts.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 18.04.060.C, open and civic space design (Ord. 804-23, 2023) (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)

fact: Renaissance Park in Evans's Tuscany subdivision has an inclusive playground the city describes as brand new as of September 2025.
quote: This park in the Tuscany Subdivision features a brand new (as of September 2025) inclusive playground, picnic shelter and a large open area for play.
source_label: City of Evans, Parks (Renaissance Park, 3501 Sienna Avenue)

fact: Hunter's Reserve Park, which Evans opened in October 2025, has a small playground structure with a nature play area, and its north side remains a stormwater detention pond.
quote: This new park - opened in October 2025 - features a walking trail, connection to the Hunter's Reserve neighborhood via Dove Lane, a small playground structure with nature play area, landscaped lawn and decomposed granite walking trail. The north side will remain as a detention pond for the City's stormwater infrastructure.
source_label: City of Evans, Parks (Hunter's Reserve Park, 3800 29th Ave.)

fact: Ridge Park in The Ridge at Prairie View has a custom-designed tower and climbing playground and a soccer-sized open turf area.
quote: Ridge Park has a brand new, custom designed tower and climbing playground that is the best play structure in the City. There is also ample parking, one large pavilion and four small pavilions. It also has a large soccer-sized open turf area.
source_label: City of Evans, Parks (Ridge Park, 2426 Bluebells Drive)
notes: 'Open turf' on the city page is not identified as artificial; do not say it is.

fact: Evans keeps home occupations indoors, in an accessory building or in the garage, except as required for state-licensed in-home family child care, and exempts child drop-off from its limits of one customer vehicle and ten client visits a week.
quote: All activity shall be conducted within an enclosed living area, accessory building, or the garage, except as required for state-licensed in-home family child care. … No more than one customer vehicle parked at the property at a time, except for drop off of children for child care or instruction; b. No more than ten (10) client visits per week, except for drop off of children for child care or instruction.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 18.02.040.K, home occupations (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)

fact: Evans defines a day care center as child care that does not meet the state definition of a family child care home, and allows one by right in the C-1, C-2 and C-3 districts and by special use permit in the R-1E, R-1, R-2, R-3, RMH and R-C districts.
quote: Day care center - an establishment that provides care for children that does not meet the State definition of a "family child care home."
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 18.02.020, allowed uses, Table 18-2-1 (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)
notes: Table 18-2-1 row 'Day care center': blank AG, PF; S in R1E, R1, R2, R3, RMH, RC; ■ in C1, C2, C3; blank C4, I1-I3 (read cell by cell 2026-09-25).

fact: On April 21, 2026 the Evans City Council passed on second reading an ordinance adding Section 18.08.080 to the landscape chapter to implement state-mandated landscaping requirements.
quote: The following Ordinance passed on the second reading at a regular meeting of the Evans City Council held on April 21, 2026. … ORDINANCE NO. 858-26 AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CHAPTER 18.08 OF THE EVANS MUNICIPAL CODE BY ADDING SECTION 18.08.080 TO IMPLEMENT CERTAIN STATE MANDATED LANDSCAPING REQUIREMENTS
source_label: City of Evans legal notice, Ordinance No. 858-26 (adds Sec. 18.08.080), second reading April 21, 2026
notes: The notice carries the title only; the April 7, 2026 council post calls it 'Ordinance No..858-26 implementing state mandated landscaping requirements'. Municode lists 858-26 in OrdBank, not yet codified (online code runs through Ord. 855-26). The text of 18.08.080 was not read: packets sit on evanscolorado.primegov.com, which did not resolve on 2026-09-25, and events.evanscolorado.gov returned 403. Whether it defines functional turf or amends the 18.08.020 common-area sentence is unknown.

fact: In the Evans Municipal Code as codified through Ord. No. 855-26 of January 6, 2026, artificial turf appears only in Sec. 18.08.020 and the word nonfunctional does not appear (searched September 25, 2026).
quote: Municode full-text search of the Evans Municipal Code (codified through Ordinance No. 855-26, adopted January 6, 2026): "artificial turf" — 1 hit (18.08.020 Landscape design: "Artificial turf is not acceptable for public or common areas."); "nonfunctional" — 0 hits; "synthetic" — 3 hits, none about turf; "putting green" — 0 hits.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code on Municode (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026; Supp. 28 posted June 2026)
notes: OrdBank on 2026-09-25 lists 2026 ordinances 858, 860, 861, 863, 865, 866, 867 and 868 as not yet codified; 858-26 adds 18.08.080 (state landscaping).

fact: Evans landscape plans must limit high-irrigation turf and plantings to high-use areas with high visibility and functional needs, and use water-conserving or drought-tolerant grasses.
quote: Limit high-irrigation turf and plantings to appropriate high-use areas with high visibility and functional needs and use water-conserving or drought-tolerant grasses.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 18.08.050.B, water conservation (Ord. 804-23, 2023) (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)

fact: Evans requires new development in areas the City Council designates to build a non-potable irrigation system for all lots and common areas, dedicate the water rights to run it, and turn the system over to the City.
quote: All new development within those areas of the Urban Growth Boundary of the City, designated by the City Council as suitable for the construction of non-potable/dual water systems, shall be required, as part of any subdivision process, to construct a non-potable/dual water system for irrigation of all lots and common areas within the subdivision. Likewise, proponents of all new development shall provide for adequate non-potable water rights dedication in amounts sufficient in both quantities and quality to operate said system so the system will provide an assured and sufficient amount of water to adequately irrigate all lots and common areas. … Therefore, the public improvements developer's agreement must provide for the transfer of such water resources, as well as the water acquisition and distribution system, to the City upon completion of said improvements and completion of the warranty period.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 13.06.010, non-potable/dual water systems (Ord. 594-14, 2014) (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)
notes: 13.06.010.C: the City operates, repairs and maintains the system after the warranty period. The 2026 GLIC cutover (evans-glic-cutover-2026) moved city-run non-potable systems outside two neighborhoods to potable water.

fact: Evans requires common open space of 4 acres per 1,000 people in residential subdivisions over 5 acres or 20 units, and 5% to 12% of the site in commercial subdivisions depending on size.
quote: Common Open Space … 4 acres / 1,000 people (for all projects over 5 acres or 20 units) … Less than 5 acres: 5% · 5 to 20 acres: 8% · 20+ acres: 12%
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 18.04.050, Table 18-4-2 required open space (Ord. 804-23, 2023) (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)
notes: Table 18-4-2 also sets public open space of 3.25 acres (neighborhood) and 2.5 acres (community) per 1,000 people for residential subdivisions. Common open space for 'C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4, or only commercial uses in R-C'.

fact: Riverside Park, Evans's park on the South Platte River, has four ball fields, two of them lighted, beside a 7-acre fishing lake.
quote: This park features a 7-acre fishing lake, over two miles of scenic trails, fishing docks, four ball fields (two lighted and two unlighted), a spacious playground area, a picnic pavilion, basketball court, pickleball court, restrooms, and many acres of undeveloped open space along the South Platte River.
source_label: City of Evans, Parks (Riverside Park, 4000 Riverside Parkway)

fact: On July 21, 2026 the Evans City Council held a public hearing on a second amendment to the consolidated service plan for Liberty Draw Metropolitan Districts 1 through 9.
quote: Public Hearing: Consideration of Resolution No. 19-2026 Approving the second amendment to the consolidated service plan for Liberty Draw Metropolitan District Nos. 1-9.
source_label: City of Evans news post, July 21, 2026: City Council meeting agenda
notes: Agenda preview; outcome not read.

fact: Evans's animal code counts as pet animals dogs, cats, rabbits, guinea pigs, hamsters, mice, snakes, iguanas, turtles, pot belly pigs, pygmy goats, ferrets and similar animals kept for the household's enjoyment rather than for sale.
quote: Pet animals means domestic dog, domestic cat, rabbit, guinea pig, hamster, mouse, snake, iguana, turtle, pot belly pig, pygmy goat, ferret and similar animal provided they are for the enjoyment of the occupants of the lot and are not kept primarily for the purpose of sale or commercial endeavor.
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 6.04.010, definitions (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)
notes: Ord. No. 867-26, amending Chapter 6.04, passed second reading on July 21, 2026 and is not yet in the online code; its text was not available to read.

fact: Evans exempts movable accessory structures of 120 square feet or less, under 10 feet high and not on a foundation or slab from its residential design standards if they sit well back from, or out of view of, public space, while larger ones must meet the design standards for the house.
quote: Minor accessory structures one hundred twenty (120) square feet or less, less than ten (10) feet high, and not on a foundation or slab shall be movable, are subject to meeting all easement conditions, and are not subject to the design standards in Chapters 18.05 or 18.06 , provided they are: a. Setback more than eight (80) feet from any public right-of-way or public space; or b. Otherwise not visible from any public right-of-way or public space due to the location and orientation of the principal structure. … For residential and commercial accessory structures over one hundred twenty (120) square feet, the design shall meet all applicable design standards for a principal building
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 18.02.040.C, accessory structures (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)
notes: The code text reads "eight (80) feet"; the word and the numeral disagree, so copy should not state the setback distance. This section is about design standards, not building permits.

fact: The Liberty Draw architectural guidelines for single-family detached homes in Evans (updated September 25, 2024) allow artificial turf in back yards, require sodded front yards, keep dog runs at least 5 feet from any property line and screened from neighboring lots, allow no more than 3 dogs or 3 cats and 4 household pets in total, require all exterior irrigation to tie into the non-potable system, and require ARC approval for dog runs, play and sports equipment, playhouses and swing sets.
quote: The guidelines are general regulations; the Architectural Review Committee (“ARC”) may grant variances to any of the guidelines based on architectural merit. … Liberty Draw Architectural Guidelines Updated September 25, 2024 … 10. Dog runs. Dog runs shall not be located within five (5) feet from any property line, and shall be screened by approved materials so that the dog run is not visible from neighboring lots. ARC approval is required for all screened dog runs. … c. Front yards must be sodded; no seeding is allowed in front yards. … e. Artificial turf may be installed in back yards. … 23. Irrigation systems. … All exterior irrigation must be tied into the non-potable system. … 33. Pets. Household pets are defined as dogs and cats. No more than 3 dogs or 3 cats with a total number of 4 household pets will be allowed. … 34. Play and sports equipment. ARC approval is required. 35. Playhouses. ARC approval is required. Basic design, materials and colors must match the residence and they are to be incorporated into and at least partially screened by landscaping features or approved fencing. … 44. Swing sets. ARC approval is required.
source_label: Liberty Draw Metropolitan District Nos. 1-9: Evans, Colorado Single Family Detached Home Architectural Guidelines (updated Sept. 25, 2024)
notes: PDF read 2026-09-25 from the district site (libertydrawsmds.com, Documents). Governs Liberty Draw single-family lots only, not the rest of Evans. Landscaping plans also need ARC approval before work starts (item 4.e).

fact: Evans makes it unlawful to let an animal kept in a yard bark, howl or make other loud and persistent noise that reasonable people would consider excessive or continuous, and lets officers impound the animal on a complaint when the owner is away.
quote: It is unlawful for the owner, keeper, harborer, or any other person who has assumed the responsibility for an animal, to permit such animal kept in any yard, house or other place to bark, howl, yelp, bawl or make other loud and persistent noise, in a manner which, under nonmitigating circumstances, could be considered by reasonable persons of ordinary sensibilities as excessive or continuous. … The code enforcement officer, police officer, or other designated officer of the City shall have authority, without liability, to use all reasonable means to abate such nuisance, including the authority to impound such animal, upon receipt of a complaint, where the owner is absent from the premises
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Sec. 6.04.150, noisy animals (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026; before Ord. 867-26)
notes: Read via the Municode API on 2026-09-25. Ord. No. 867-26 (July 21, 2026) amends Chapter 6.04 and is not yet codified; re-read once it is.

fact: Evans allows dogs off leash only inside designated off-leash dog parks, under voice control and in sight of the owner, and requires owners to pick up after them there; elsewhere in city parks a dog must be on a leash of 10 feet or less.
quote: Dogs may be allowed off-leash only within designated off-leash dog parks in the City. Dogs must be under voice control and in sight of the owner at all times and owners must follow all posted rules and regulations while in the dog park. Any owner, taking the animal in to any dog park, shall immediately remove or cause to be removed and lawfully dispose of all fecal matter left on such property by the animal. … Controlled dogs are allowed on City-owned parks, trails and open space. A controlled dog must be on a leash ten (10) feet or less in length, attached to the dog and held by or tied to a person
source_label: Evans Municipal Code Secs. 16.40.111 and 16.40.112, dogs in parks and off-leash dog park (codified through Ord. No. 855-26, Jan. 6, 2026)
notes: Found by Municode full-text search for "dog park" (1 hit) on 2026-09-25. The code does not name which parks are designated.

fact: Evans's posted watering restrictions set lawn-watering days by address and property type and bar outdoor watering from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.; the page does not mention hosing down hard surfaces, pens or artificial turf.
quote: Single-family homes with even-numbered addresses shall only water lawns on Sunday, Tuesday, and Thursday … Single-family homes with odd-numbered addresses shall only water lawns on Monday, Wednesday, and Saturday … Multi-family residences, apartments and commercial properties shall only water lawns on Sunday, Tuesday, and Friday … Outdoor watering is allowed on scheduled days except between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.
source_label: City of Evans, Watering Restrictions and Seasonal Recommendations (read September 25, 2026)
notes: Restrictions sit under the April 21, 2026 drought emergency (Res. 05-2026) and Emergency Ord. 860-26 on water conservation, whose text was not read.

fact: Next door to Evans, the City of Greeley runs two courses with practice greens: Highland Hills has two practice putting greens and a short game area, and Boomerang Links has one large practice putting green and a smaller chipping green.
quote: In addition, there are two practice putting greens and a short game area to help golfers improve all areas of the game and ultimately lower scores. … Boomerang Links has one large practice putting green and a smaller chipping green to help hone your short game skills.
source_label: City of Greeley Golf, Highland Hills and Boomerang Links course pages (read September 25, 2026)
notes: Second quote from https://greeleyco.gov/golf/courses/boomerang-links/. The Highland Hills page gives both "opened in 1959" and "since 1964"; this record uses neither.
